title: Paper Town
description: Follow one man's wages backwards and see how far out of the valley they go before anyone's name is on them.

whose_wages.title: Who pays the chainman
whose_wages.objective: Ask Alder Pyke who actually pays him.
whose_wages.journal: Pyke draws one and threepence a day at the Rivermark counting house. The counting house is not paying it. It is honouring a note for somebody who is.

the_note.title: The note of hand
the_note.objective: The wages are drawn at the counting house. Go and read what they are drawn on.
the_note.journal: The counting house keeps the notes it has honoured for a year before it burns them. Pyke's are in the tray with the rest, and there will be one with a mark on it instead of a name.

followed_it.title: A name, and a river
followed_it.journal: The note is drawn on a house downriver at Greyhythe and signed by its factor, and the factor's name is Ludo Corse. I have asked eleven people in Rivermark whether they have heard of him. None of them has. Six of them are, one way or another, working for him.

let_it_lie.title: Somebody's money
let_it_lie.journal: Somebody downriver is paying a chainman one and threepence a day to walk lines in a valley they do not live in. That is not a crime, it is not my business, and I have put the tray back where I found it.
